summary: Proved that paired Young-tower branching recurrences leave a fresh harmonic bipartition component at every rank and verified that exact small-degree hyperoctahedral restriction vectors use it. This kills the naive branching-only compiler but leaves structured harmonic rotations as the precise positive target.

theorem.complexity_boundary: A growing kernel and classically hard general plethysm do not imply a quantum circuit lower bound; global consistency or local harmonic rotations may recover the data efficiently.
theorem.differential_poset_identity: The product of two Young lattices obeys D_m D_m^T-D_(m-1)^T D_(m-1)=2I; hence D_m has full row rank.
theorem.exact_branching_recurrence: D_m b_m(lambda,-)[nu] = sum_gamma f^(lambda/gamma) b_(m-1)(gamma,nu), by restricting through K_m or S_(2m-2).
theorem.finite_natural_witness: Exact inner-size-two plethysm controls show every tested actual restriction vector has nonzero orthogonal projection to ker D_m.
theorem.positive_compiler_target: Construct a source-aware maximal commutant algebra and local rotations that propagate the harmonic component coherently.
theorem.underdetermination: The recurrence fixes only the down image and leaves a kernel of dimension p_2(m)-p_2(m-1) at every rank.

theorem_contract.claim_boundary: Failure of the naive lower-rank recurrence, not hardness of all coherent subduction transforms.
